name: ERC-238
question: Does daily intravaginal prasterone improve dyspareunia and vaginal atrophy measures versus a matching placebo insert in postmenopausal women?

design.population: Postmenopausal women aged 40–80 years with moderate-to-severe dyspareunia as their most bothersome vulvovaginal atrophy symptom, vaginal pH above 5, and 5% or fewer superficial cells.
design.description: Multicenter double-blind 2:1 randomized placebo-controlled superiority trial
design.locator: Primary report, Methods (Inclusion criteria; Randomization); ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02013544, Participant Flow (558 randomized; 376 prasterone, 182 placebo)

verdictNote: All four coprimary endpoints met the prespecified two-sided 0.05 threshold at 12 weeks.
takeaway: In ERC-238, daily intravaginal prasterone 6.5 mg improved dyspareunia and all three coprimary vaginal cytology/pH measures versus a matching placebo insert after 12 weeks in postmenopausal women with symptomatic vulvovaginal atrophy.

reports.label: Sexual-function analysis
reports.citation: Labrie F, Derogatis L, Archer DF, et al. Effect of Intravaginal Prasterone on Sexual Dysfunction in Postmenopausal Women with Vulvovaginal Atrophy. *J Sex Med.* 2015;12(12):2401-2412.

results.endpoint: Female Sexual Function Index total score
results.measure: Baseline-adjusted difference in total-score change at 12 weeks, prasterone minus placebo
results.note: Total scores were calculable for 300/325 prasterone and 149/157 placebo recipients in the defined ITT population; missing satisfaction responses prevented calculation for some women. The report describes no confidence interval or multiplicity adjustment.
results.locator: Full text, Results, pp 2406–2408, Figure 7; Methods (Statistical Analysis), p 2403

results.endpoint: Female Sexual Function Index desire domain
results.measure: 12-week mean desire score; baseline-adjusted difference in change, prasterone minus placebo
results.note: Secondary FSFI analysis in women enrolled for vulvovaginal atrophy with dyspareunia, not for a diagnosis of hypoactive sexual desire disorder.
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 2405, Figure 1; Discussion, p 2409

results.endpoint: Female Sexual Function Index pain domain
results.measure: 12-week mean pain-domain score; baseline-adjusted difference in change, prasterone minus placebo
results.note: Higher FSFI pain-domain scores indicate better sexual function; this is separate from the primary dyspareunia severity score.

reports.label: 12-week pivotal report
reports.dateLocator: Crossref published-print March 2016; PubMed/Europe PMC publication status ppublish and March 2016 issue (day not supplied)
reports.citation: Labrie F, Archer DF, Koltun W, et al. Efficacy of intravaginal dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA) on moderate to severe dyspareunia and vaginal dryness, symptoms of vulvovaginal atrophy, and of the genitourinary syndrome of menopause. *Menopause.* 2016;23(3):243-256.

results.measure: 12-week mean score on a 0–3 scale; adjusted mean difference in score units, prasterone minus placebo
results.note: ANCOVA adjusted for baseline; decreases from baseline were 1.42 and 1.06 units.
results.locator: Primary report, Results (pain at sexual activity), Figure 5

results.measure: 12-week mean proportion; adjusted mean difference in percentage points, prasterone minus placebo
results.note: ANCOVA adjusted for baseline; adjusted difference differs from subtraction of displayed endpoint means.

results.measure: 12-week mean proportion; adjusted mean difference in percentage points, prasterone minus placebo
results.note: Adjusted difference stated in the report abstract; endpoint means in Results/Figure 3.
results.locator: Primary report, Abstract (Results); Results (superficial cells), Figure 3

results.measure: 12-week mean vaginal pH; adjusted mean difference in pH units, prasterone minus placebo
results.note: Difference stated in the report abstract; endpoint means in Results/Figure 4.
results.locator: Primary report, Abstract (Results); Results (vaginal pH), Figure 4

results.measure: 12-week mean score among women with moderate-to-severe dryness at baseline; adjusted mean difference in score units
results.note: Prespecified hierarchical secondary endpoint, tested after dyspareunia; change from baseline was −1.44 versus −1.17.
results.locator: Primary report, Statistical analysis; Results (vaginal dryness), Figure 6

harms.label: Application-site vaginal discharge
harms.note: Two women discontinued treatment because of discharge.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.note: Treatment-emergent events; no inferential comparison reported.

delivery.label: Efficacy-analysis population
delivery.value: 482/558 randomized women (325/376 prasterone; 157/182 placebo) entered the prespecified efficacy analysis; 72 treated women failed at least one baseline entry criterion despite meeting screening criteria.
delivery.locator: Primary report, Methods (Analysis populations), Disposition of participants; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT02013544, Participant Flow

delivery.label: Treatment regimen
delivery.value: One 0.50% prasterone (6.5 mg) or matching placebo vaginal ovule nightly using a single-use applicator for 12 weeks.

delivery.label: Completed study in efficacy population
delivery.note: These are study completion, not dose-adherence, figures.
